subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Challenger Disaster: O-Rings in the Cold
description: A fast breakdown of The Challenger Disaster: O-Rings in the Cold for builders.

hook.text: On January 28, 1986, the Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch. All seven crew members died.

buildup.text: The launch temperature was 36 degrees F — 15 degrees colder than any previous launch. Ice hung from the launch pad.

discovery.text: An O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster failed in the cold. Hot gas burned through the joint and ignited the fuel tank.

twist.text: Morton Thiokol engineers warned NASA the night before. Management overruled them under schedule pressure. The launch proceeded.

climax.text: The Rogers Commission found NASA's decision-making culture was the root cause. Technical warnings were suppressed by management.

punchline.text: Engineers said don't launch. Managers said launch. The O-ring agreed with the engineers.

quiz.question: Why did the Challenger's O-ring fail on the day of launch?
options: The O-ring material was defective from the manufacturing process
Cold temperatures made the rubber O-ring too stiff to seal properly
Vibrations during ignition dislodged the O-ring from its groove
